newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdynia shipyard to sell 40 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdynia shipyard to sell 40 pct stake.

text.p: Poland's state-owned Gdynia shipyard plans to offer this year a 39.9-percent stake to a strategic investor, the firm's president said on Thursdsay.
Krzysztof Banaszak told Reuters this would be done through a new issue of 10 million preferred shares at a minimum issue price of 20 zlotys.
It would give the investor 51.5 percent of votes at the general shareholders' meeting.
"The Gdynia shipyard plans to sell almost 40 percent of shares to a strategic investor, which would give the investor more than 51 percent of votes," he said.
He added the shipyard had held talks with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on taking the stake, but declined to give any details.
The shipyard would also like the state treasury to offer six million shares or a 18.4-percent stake in the yard to Gdynia's employees. The treasury now has 46 percent of Gdynia.
Among Gdynia's other shareholders are the state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA which has 20.5 percent of shares and Bank Handlowy SA 18.7 percent.
In the January-October period the shipyard had a loss of 60.3 million zlotys ($20.8 million).
This year the shipyard expects to record a 7-million-zloty ($2.4 million) net profit on $392 million sales.

After the new issue and the taking of shares by employees the investor would have 39.9 percent of shares, employees 18 percent, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA 12.3 percent, Bank Handlowy 11.2 percent and the shipyard's management five percent.
The state treasury would hold the remaining shares.
